newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Shining Path attacks village, kills two.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Shining Path attacks village, kills two.

text.p: About 150 Maoist guerrillas from Peru's Shining Path movement have attacked a jungle village, killing a policeman's sister and her daughter, police said on Tuesday.
The rebels also stole goods and painted slogans during Sunday's assault on the village of Santa Lucia, in the Huallaga Valley jungle zone 280 miles (450 km) northeast of Lima.

Police in nearby Tingo Maria said the guerrilla band shot Adelaida Alvarado, 38, because her brother was an anti-terrorist policeman. Her daughter Merelyn Camacho, 4, was killed because she started crying, the Lima daily El Comercio reported.
The guerrillas tied up Alvarado's husband Lorenzo Camacho but he escaped into the jungle when their attention was distracted by an approaching vehicle, the newspaper said.

Shining Path has been weakened since the 1992 capture of its leader Abimael Guzman and overshadowed in recent months by the takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima by its smaller rival, the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
But Shining Path remains the strongest guerrilla movement in Peru, where guerrilla wars have taken 30,000 lives since 1980.
